<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire.io/trails/764
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Adds `GET /api/v1/trails/:host/:owner/:repo/:number/code-review/stream` — a Server-Sent Events endpoint that tails a Trail's code review (live discussion thread) in near-real time. Emits an initial replay of existing comments, then per-poll diffs for additions, edits, and deletions.

This unblocks an `entire trail watch` CLI subcommand (follow-up branch) and a frontend live code-review view.

### Naming note

"Code review" here is the conversational thread on a Trail — the back-and-forth between author and reviewers stored in `repo_trails.discussion`. It is intentionally distinct from the existing `POST /review` / `GET /reviews` endpoints, which record formal **approve / request-changes** verdicts stored in `repo_trails.reviews`. The SSE event payloads still use `comment` / `comment_deleted` because each item flowing over the wire is a comment within the review.

## Design highlights

- **Bounded stream lifetime (~50s)** to stay within Cloudflare Workers request limits. Closes with `event: reconnect` so `EventSource` auto-reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`.
- **Resume semantics**: `Last-Event-ID` header *or* `?replay=false` query pre-seeds the dedup map with current state and only emits changes from that point. The `ready` event also carries an `id:` line so resume works before any comment event has fired.
- **~1s polling cadence**, with discussion-JSON parse skipped when `repo_trails.updated_at` is unchanged.
- **Abort-aware sleep** so client disconnects close the stream in <50ms, not up to 1s.
- **Per-isolate concurrency caps** (5 streams/user, 1 per (user, trail)) enforced via a small in-isolate registry; excess connections get HTTP 429. Explicitly documented as a stop-gap before DO-based fan-out.
- **Structured per-stream observability**: OTEL span attributes (`trail.code_review_stream.*`) plus a single greppable log line on close with reason, duration, polls, events.
- **Strongly-typed event payloads** (`TrailCodeReviewStream*Payload` interfaces) exported for CLI/frontend consumers; OpenAPI description documents all 6 event types with examples.

## Event types

`ready`, `comment`, `comment_deleted`, `reconnect`, `deleted`, `error`, plus SSE `: ping` keepalives every ~15s. See `docs/trail-code-review-stream.md` for the full spec.

## Tests

| Suite | Status |
|-------|--------|
| `api/src/routes/trails.test.ts` (11 SSE cases) | ✅ |
| `api/src/lib/trail-code-review-stream-registry.test.ts` (5 cases) | ✅ |
| `api/test/trail-code-review-stream.test.ts` (3 integration cases, real MySQL) | ✅ |
| `pnpm run api:test:unit` (full unit suite) | ✅ 1525 passed |
| `pnpm --filter entire-api run lint` | ✅ 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `pnpm run format:check` | ✅ |

The integration test asserts the full round-trip: connect with a real `ent_` API token → drain initial replay → write to `repo_trails.discussion` directly in MySQL → observe the new `comment` event over the same connection.

The full `pnpm run api:test` shows 33 pre-existing failures in `repo-sync-service.test.ts` and `sessions.test.ts` that exist on `main` (verified by `git stash` + re-run); this PR introduces no new failures.

## Docs

- **`docs/trail-code-review-stream.md`** is the client-facing spec: lifecycle, all 6 event payloads, resume semantics, performance characteristics, CLI implementation notes (incl. Node `EventSource` `Last-Event-ID` quirks).
- The OpenAPI route description mirrors the doc, including SSE response examples.

## Out of scope (explicit follow-ups)

- **CLI client** with reconnect + `Last-Event-ID` propagation.
- **Durable Object fan-out** so a hot trail with N viewers costs one DB poll, not N.
- **Strict `Last-Event-ID` parsing** (currently used as a binary "skip replay" flag — sufficient for code-review comments, where dedup rebuilds from current state on connect).

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] Lint
- [x] Format
- [x] API unit tests
- [x] Integration test against real MySQL
- [x] Docs

> 
> **Overview**
> Adds `GET /api/v1/trails/:host/:owner/:repo/:number/code-review/stream`, a Server-Sent Events endpoint that **streams Trail discussion comment activity** (initial `ready`, optional replay, then incremental `comment` / `comment_deleted` diffs) with keepalive pings and a forced ~50s reconnect cycle to fit Worker request limits.

# Trail Code-Review SSE Stream

Tail a Trail's code review (discussion comments) in near-real time over Server-Sent Events.

> Naming note: "code review" here refers to the live discussion thread on a Trail — the back-and-forth between author and reviewers. It is distinct from the structured `POST /review` / `GET /reviews` endpoints that record formal approve / request-changes verdicts.

- **Endpoint**: `GET /api/v1/trails/:host/:owner/:repo/:number/code-review/stream`
- **Auth**: Same as the rest of `/api/v1/trails/*` — Bearer token (`ent_…` API token sent via `Authorization: Bearer …`) **and** `users.is_admin = 1` (`requireAdmin`). Non-admins receive `403`.
- **Content type**: `text/event-stream`.
- **Implementation**: `api/src/routes/trails.ts` (`code_review_stream` route).

This document is the source of truth for client implementations (CLI, frontend). The OpenAPI description for the route mirrors this content.

## Why polling SSE (and not push)?

The current implementation polls `repo_trails.getById` every ~1s and emits diffs. This is intentionally simple and has known scaling limits (one DB query per second per connected client). The long-term plan is a Durable Object that owns the subscription and broadcasts to N subscribers. Until then, the per-isolate concurrency caps below keep a single Worker from being overwhelmed.

## Lifecycle

```
client connect
  ├── 200 OK, Content-Type: text/event-stream
  ├── event: ready                       ← always first
  ├── event: comment   (× N)             ← initial replay (suppressed in resume mode)
  ├── …
  ├── event: comment | comment_deleted   ← as the trail changes
  ├── : ping                              ← keepalive every ~15s of idle time
  └── one of:
      ├── event: deleted     → trail row was deleted; stream closes
      ├── event: reconnect   → max stream duration reached; client should reconnect
      └── event: error       → unrecoverable server-side error
```

The server caps each connection at **~50 seconds** to stay within Cloudflare Workers request limits. Clients must be prepared to reconnect — either via the browser `EventSource` auto-reconnect (which automatically resends the last `id:` as `Last-Event-ID`) or by re-issuing the request manually.

## Resume semantics

Pass either:

- `Last-Event-ID: <id>` HTTP header, **or**
- `?replay=false` query parameter

…to skip the initial replay. The server seeds its dedup state with the current trail discussion and only emits **changes from this point forward**.

> **Note**: `Last-Event-ID` is currently used as a binary "skip replay" flag. The server does not parse the value — it does not need to, because the dedup map is rebuilt from current state on every connect. This means: if a comment's content was edited and reverted while you were disconnected, you will not see those events on reconnect. For threaded review comments this is acceptable; if you need exactly-once event delivery, switch to the (future) DO-backed implementation.

## Event types

All named events carry a JSON `data:` payload. Only `ready`, `comment`, and `comment_deleted` include an `id:` line (those are the events a client may want to resume from). The terminal-ish events `reconnect`, `deleted`, and `error` are sent without an `id:` — on reconnect, clients should send the last `id:` they saw from a `ready`/`comment`/`comment_deleted` frame. The `: ping` keepalive is a bare SSE comment with no event/data/id.

### `ready`

Emitted exactly once, immediately after connect.

```jsonc
{
  "repo": "acme/web",
  "trailNumber": 42,
  "updatedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "commentCount": 1,
  "resumed": false, // true when Last-Event-ID or ?replay=false suppressed replay
}
```

`id`: `<updatedAtMs>:ready`.

### `comment`

Emitted for each existing comment during initial replay (unless suppressed) and whenever a comment is added or edited.

```jsonc
{
  "repo": "acme/web",
  "trailNumber": 42,
  "updatedAt": "2026-01-01T00:01:40Z",
  "comment": {
    /* full TrailComment, including nested replies */
  },
}
```

`id`: `<updatedAtMs>:<commentId>`. Unchanged comments are not re-emitted on subsequent polls (dedup is signature-based: `JSON.stringify(comment)`).

### `comment_deleted`

Emitted when a comment present in a previous frame is no longer in the trail's discussion.

```jsonc
{
  "repo": "acme/web",
  "trailNumber": 42,
  "updatedAt": "2026-01-01T00:02:00Z",
  "commentId": "c2",
}
```

`id`: `<updatedAtMs>:<commentId>:deleted`.

### `reconnect`

Emitted just before the server closes the stream because the max stream duration was reached. No `id:` line. Reconnect immediately and pass the most recent `id:` line you saw (from a `ready`/`comment`/`comment_deleted` frame) as `Last-Event-ID` (or use `?replay=false`). Today the only `reason` is `max_duration`.

```jsonc
{
  "repo": "acme/web",
  "trailNumber": 42,
  "reason": "max_duration",
}
```

### `deleted`

Emitted when the underlying Trail row is deleted while you're connected. No `id:` line. The stream closes immediately after this event. Clients should not auto-reconnect.

```jsonc
{ "repo": "acme/web", "trailNumber": 42 }
```

### `error`

Emitted when the polling loop hits an unrecoverable server-side error (e.g. DB outage). No `id:` line. The stream closes immediately. The `message` is intentionally generic — the underlying error (DB query fragment, connection details, etc.) is recorded server-side via OTEL spans and the structured close log line, never sent to the client. Clients should treat `error` as "reconnect".

```jsonc
{ "message": "Stream error — please reconnect" }
```

### `: ping`

A bare SSE comment line (`: ping <epochMs>\n\n`). Sent every ~15 seconds of idle time so intermediaries don't close the connection. No `event:` or `data:`. Clients should ignore it.

## Concurrency limits

Per Worker isolate (not global):

- **5** concurrent streams per user.
- **1** concurrent stream per (user, trail).

Excess connections receive `429 Too Many Requests` with `{ "error": "<reason>" }`. These limits are a safeguard against runaway clients and assume a typical client only needs one tail per trail. The right long-term fix is fan-out via a Durable Object so a hot trail with N viewers costs one DB poll, not N.

## Performance characteristics

- **Polling cadence**: ~1s. Latency floor for new events is therefore ~1s.
- **Per-connection cost**: 1 PK lookup on `repo_trails` per second + 1 small JSON parse + one diff over the comment array.
- **Skipped work**: when `repo_trails.updated_at` is unchanged, the discussion JSON is not re-parsed.
- **Max duration**: 50 seconds per connection.
- **Keepalive**: 15 seconds.
- **Memory**: O(comment count) per connection (signature dedup map).

## Observability

Every stream emits structured logs and OTEL span attributes for ops:

- **Open**: `console.log` line `[trail-code-review-stream] opened repo=<full> trail=<n> user=<id> resumed=<bool>` plus a `trail.code_review_stream.opened` span event with the same fields.
- **Close**: `console.log` (or `console.error` for the `error` reason) `[trail-code-review-stream] closed reason=<r> repo=<full> trail=<n> user=<id> duration_ms=<ms> polls=<n> events=<n>` plus a `trail.code_review_stream.closed` span event. `reason` is one of `aborted` (client disconnect), `max_duration`, `deleted`, `error`, `completed`. On `error`, the underlying exception is also fed through `recordSpanError` and surfaces as a span error status — it is **not** included in the wire payload.
- **Span attributes** (set on the active request span): `trail.stream.repo`, `trail.stream.trail_number`, `trail.stream.user_id`, `trail.stream.duration_ms`, `trail.stream.polls_run`, `trail.stream.events_sent`, `trail.stream.close_reason`, `trail.stream.resumed`.

## Testing

- Unit tests: `api/src/routes/trails.test.ts` (100 cases total, ~14 dedicated to the SSE stream).
- Registry tests: `api/src/lib/trail-code-review-stream-registry.test.ts` (5 cases).
- Integration test (real MySQL): `api/test/trail-code-review-stream.test.ts` (3 cases, incl. a real-DB write → wire round-trip). Run with `pnpm run api:test` after `mise run api-db-start`.

## Client implementation notes

- Browsers: `EventSource` works out of the box, but cannot set `Authorization`. Use a fetch-based polyfill or move auth into a cookie / proxy.
- Node / CLI: native `EventSource` (Node 22+) does not consistently propagate `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect — prefer the `eventsource` npm package, or hand-roll a fetch loop that:
  1. On `event: reconnect`, reconnect immediately with no backoff.
  2. On network error, exponential backoff starting at 500ms.
  3. Send the most recently observed `id:` line as `Last-Event-ID`.
- The wire payload's `comment` object matches the `TrailComment` TypeScript type in `api/src/types.ts`. Treat the rest of the envelope as the shapes documented above.

content.text:
Done. Summary of changes:

**New `entire trail watch` subcommand** that consumes the SSE endpoint added in PR #1888 (`GET /api/v1/trails/:host/:owner/:repo/:number/code-review/stream`).

Files:
- **`cmd/entire/cli/api/client.go`** — added `Client.GetStream(ctx, path, headers)` that returns the response with body still open and supports custom request headers (needed for `Accept: text/event-stream` and `Last-Event-ID`).
- **`cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go`** — registered `newTrailWatchCmd()` under `entire trail`.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd.go`** — new command:
  - Resolves trail number from positional arg or current branch (via `findTrailByBranch`).
  - Hand-rolled SSE framing parser (per spec — colon-prefixed comments are pings, blank line dispatches an event, fields parsed: `event`, `data`, `id`, `retry` ignored).
  - Handles all six event types (`ready`, `comment`, `comment_deleted`, `reconnect`, `deleted`, `error`) plus `: ping` keepalives.
  - Auto-reconnect: immediate on `event: reconnect` (max-duration close), exponential backoff (500ms → 30s cap) on transport errors / `event: error`.
  - Tracks `Last-Event-ID` from the most recent `ready`/`comment`/`comment_deleted` frame and resends it on reconnect; falls back to `?replay=false` on the first reconnect when no id was seen.
  - Flags: `--json` (machine-readable envelopes), `--show-pings`, `--once` (drain replay and exit, deterministic via the `commentCount` from `ready`).
  - Honours `--insecure-http-auth` from the trail-root persistent flag and treats 401/403 as terminal (no auto-reconnect).
- **`cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd_test.go`** — table-style coverage of the SSE parser using `httptest`: ready+comment in `--once` mode, `--json` envelope shape, `reconnect` event preserves prior id, `Last-Event-ID` header is forwarded.

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` is clean; targeted unit tests and the full `cmd/entire/cli` + `cmd/entire/cli/api` suites pass.
